A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Slot Interpreters. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reordering and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original object-discovery, scene-property retrieval and few-shot classification experiments in Section 5, plus object-detection experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds bounding-box grounding comparisons, annotation-efficiency and incomplete-annotation experiments, and zero-shot Pascal VOC evaluation.

M1.justification: The visXML schema, scene and schema encoders, primitive-to-slot similarity aggregation, and combined contrastive/reconstruction objective remain unchanged. The Appendix E schema generator also already exists in v2. Calling the existing contrastive objective InfoNCE does not change its procedure.

E1.justification: The original dataset and task coverage is retained. v3 adds COCO-to-Pascal VOC 2012 zero-shot object discovery and retrieval with incomplete scene descriptions capped at five or ten annotated objects. These are limited extensions of the existing segmentation and retrieval coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.2.2 newly evaluates BBox QKV, adapted from Gupta et al. (2020), against NSI on MOVi-C and COCO. This introduces a substantive region-based weakly supervised grounding comparison absent from v2. The original retrieval, classification and detection comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds training-fraction sweeps at 1%, 10%, 50% and 100%, ground-truth bounding-box inputs for BBox QKV, InfoNCE-bound tracking, annotation caps, COCO grounding-example sweeps and zero-shot transfer evaluation. Existing splits and hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new comparison inconsistently describes its scoring control and whether the MI curves use test or validation data.

E4.justification: New analyses probe annotation efficiency, MI learning dynamics, overlapping/occluded-object grounding failures, incomplete annotations, COCO annotation-count sensitivity and cross-dataset segmentation transfer. Conversely, v2 Appendix E.3 and Figure 39's detection-versus-slot-count analysis disappears. Existing backbone, schema, property and retrieval-slot ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Retained experiments preserve their five-seed standard-deviation reporting. The added Pascal VOC rows follow the same practice. No changed run counts, significance-testing procedures or uncertainty-estimation methods are documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds BBox QKV comparisons, annotation-scarcity and incomplete-annotation retrieval results, MI-bound curves and transfer results. Table 6 adds Pascal VOC zero-shot FG-ARI of 21.97 ± 0.17 for NSI versus 20.42 ± 0.13 for ungrounded slots, while retaining the original segmentation values. The detection slot-count results from v2 Figure 39 are removed.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4.2.4 adds a mathematical definition of scene-schema mutual information and an argument connecting the symmetric InfoNCE objective to MI ≥ log(B) − Lcontrastive in Equations 14–16. This theoretical justification is absent from v2; the existing method equations remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion add central claims that learned slot representations ground object semantics better than conventional bounding-box representations and generalize better under fixed or reduced annotation budgets. The earlier claims about grounding, object discovery and few-shot reasoning are retained.

C2.justification: v3 attributes bounding-box failures to overlap and occlusion, explains NSI's advantages through finer object masks, and interprets higher InfoNCE bounds as stronger semantic-information capture. It also adds explanations for incomplete-annotation resilience and structural transfer between datasets, substantially extending v2's interpretation of the evidence.

D1.justification: v3 documents implementation choices for the new BBox QKV adaptation: replacing phrase embeddings with schema representations, adding query/key/value attention heads, and supplying ground-truth regions. Existing architecture hyperparameters, Nvidia A100 hardware disclosures and training-cost tables in Appendices C and E are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantial Visual Grounding discussion positioning NSI against vision-language pretraining, region-based weak supervision and neuro-symbolic approaches. New references include Gupta et al. (2020), Karpathy and Fei-Fei (2015), GroupViT and contrastive predictive coding. This materially broadens the research context beyond v2's positioning.

P1.justification: Grounding experiments move ahead of object discovery in both the main text and Appendix D. The introduction and contribution list are restructured, retrieval receives a new subsection hierarchy, preliminaries are expanded, and several results discussions are substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 changes document-wide typography and layout, relocates retained figures, expands Table 6, and adds comparison and robustness displays. The classification figure is reformatted without changing its results, and the schema-generator diagram expands from v2 Figure 35 to v3 Figure 40. v2 Figure 39 is removed.

improvement.justification: v3 better tests NSI's practical grounding advantages through a region-based comparator, annotation-scarcity and incompleteness checks, and cross-dataset transfer, addressing gaps in v2's validation and positioning. However, inconsistent descriptions of scoring and the MI-curve split weaken the strongest new mechanistic inference, and the detection slot-count sweep is lost. These tradeoffs make the net quality gain positive but limited.
